solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: English wrapped in endless cloth what French put on their sticks

definitions.text: what French put on their sticks

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the following word is dropped
something wrapped in a covering sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: burrel is an old coarse russet cloth
standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A Frenchman with a strange habit of wrapping things in English cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: BURREL loses its last letter to give BURRE, and E goes in after the B. The 'sticks' are French loaves, baguettes.
explanation.definitionFit: Beurre is the French word for butter, which the French spread on their baguettes.

clue.text: Fancy man in Grenoble craftily producing pink flower

indicators.note: acting craftily means working things round by cunning, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a fancy man is slang for a pimp
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lover in the French city of Grenoble cunningly produces a pink bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The bog pimpernel is a small creeping wildflower of wet ground with pale pink flowers.

clue.text: Electroplated support (penny spent) is a feature of fair mug?

indicators.note: money spent is gone, so the coin named in the brackets leaves the word

blocks.note: EP is the abbreviation for electroplated
to help is to support
P is the abbreviation for a penny; it is removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plated tray-stand has lost its penny value, and the question is about a fair-skinned face.
explanation.walkthrough: HELP loses its P. A mug is slang for a face, and 'fair' means pale-skinned.
explanation.definitionFit: An ephelis is a freckle, the kind of spot typically found on a pale complexion.

clue.text: Upper-class folio on dull study of transport?

blocks.note: U is the standard abbreviation for upper-class
fo is a printers' abbreviation for folio
logy is an American word for sluggish or dull

explanation.surface: A posh book volume rests on some dreary account of transport studies.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'transport' is the flying saucer that supposedly carries aliens about; the question mark flags the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ufology is the study of unidentified flying objects, imagined as craft that ferry visitors from space.

clue.text: Comeback concerning damaging wrong?

blocks.note: re means concerning or about
in law a tort is a civil wrong that causes damage

explanation.surface: A sharp reply about some harmful misdeed.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is a quick, sharp reply, which is what a comeback is in conversation.

clue.text: Wrap up engraving on particularly rounded branch

blocks.note: eng. is the abbreviation for engraving
a lobe is a rounded projection or division, as of a leaf

explanation.surface: Finishing off an engraving of a branch with rounded tips.
explanation.definitionFit: To englobe is to enclose completely as if in a globe, that is, to wrap up entirely.

clue.text: Breaking golden rule could find this cheat done

indicators.note: something broken is smashed into pieces, so the words are jumbled
the jumble is split into the wanted word and a leftover, which this phrasing sets apart

blocks.note: taken as written
these letters are the leftover, taken out

explanation.surface: Break the golden rule of ethics and you might find yourself cheated.
explanation.walkthrough: A subtractive anagram: the letters of 'golden rule' rearranged make the answer plus DONE. 'Done' also means cheated, which knits the surface together.
explanation.definitionFit: A guller is one who gulls, a deceiver or cheat who dupes the gullible.

clue.text: Rampant spruce overshadowing English plants

indicators.note: a rampant beast rears up on its hind legs, so in a down clue the word climbs upwards
to overshadow is to loom over and enclose, so one piece is wrapped around the other

blocks.note: smug can mean neat, trim or spruce
standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A spruce tree growing wildly and casting shade over English plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spruce' looks like the tree but is the adjective for trim; reversed it gives GUMS, which goes round E.
explanation.definitionFit: Geums are a genus of herbaceous plants of the rose family, often called avens.

clue.text: Last in Utah, decent having ceded what's core

indicators.note: giving up its core means the middle letters of the word are surrendered

blocks.note: UT is the postal abbreviation for Utah
modest means decent, decorous; its central pair goes

explanation.surface: Someone seeming decent in Utah gives up what lies at the heart of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last in Utah' tempts you to take the final letter H; instead 'Last' is the definition and 'in' only joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Utmost can mean last or farthest, the extreme point, as in the utmost ends of the earth.

clue.text: Landslide in this year in Libya

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: AH stands for anno hujus, Latin for in this year
LAR is Libya's international vehicle registration code

explanation.surface: A landslide hitting Libya this year.
explanation.definitionFit: A lahar is a mudflow of volcanic debris, a landslide down the slopes of a volcano.

clue.text: SNP's intention is to corral a mob apart from leader

indicators.note: everything except the leader means the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: police kettle a crowd by penning it in a confined area

explanation.surface: The Scottish National Party plans to hem in a crowd, minus its leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The SNP is the Scottish National Party, so its intention is a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ettle is a Scots word meaning to intend or purpose, so it fits a Scottish party's aim.

clue.text: Reference lexicon on papal treasury's image maker

blocks.note: ref is short for reference
lex is short for lexicon
the Camera is the papal treasury of the Vatican

explanation.surface: A reference dictionary laid on the Vatican treasury's picture-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflex camera uses a mirror to show the photographer the image, and cameras produce pictures.

clue.text: Run through quaggy peat, otherwise enter therein

indicators.note: quaggy means boggy and shifting, so the letters slide about into a new order
taken otherwise means arranged in a different way
in there means placed inside the first jumble

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A walker crossing a bog: tramp through boggy peat, or else go in.
explanation.definitionFit: To penetrate is to pierce, to pass right through something, as a sword runs one through.

clue.text: Grand present sticks in trees

blocks.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
to present a show is to host it
gum sticks things together

explanation.surface: A splendid gift gets stuck up in the branches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand present' reads as a big gift; split it into abbreviation and verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghost gums are Australian eucalyptus trees with striking white bark.

clue.text: Initially pernicious and harmful being ill-gotten gains

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of pernicious
an elf in folklore is a mischievous, often malicious sprite

explanation.surface: Money gained dishonestly is, from the start, harmful and pernicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harmful being' reads as an adjective plus a participle but is one noun phrase, a malign sprite.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelf is money or wealth, especially when acquired dishonestly, hence ill-gotten gains.

clue.text: Lofty lines on reserve force

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another comes after it, so the first-named piece is written second

blocks.note: the TA, the Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force
LL is the abbreviation for lines

explanation.surface: Grand lines of defence laid by the reserve army.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall and lofty are synonyms, both describing great height.

clue.text: Balancing box, eg, such is nailed to the mast

definitions.text: such is nailed to the mast

blocks.note: cross can mean set against or counterbalancing, as a cross entry in accounts
box is an example of a tree

explanation.surface: A box or similar piece of wood, balanced, gets nailed to a ship's mast.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the idiom 'nailed to the mast', meaning firmly committed.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosstrees are horizontal timbers fixed across the top of a ship's mast to spread the rigging.

clue.text: May, in the past, showing intensity of feeling

blocks.note: first meaning: the past tense of the verb may
second meaning: force or vigour

explanation.surface: Last May someone showed powerful emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' with its capital looks like the month or a name; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb form is the past of 'may'; the noun means power or force, as in with all one's strength.

clue.text: Dudley Do-Right's vessels stick close to waters around Quebec

blocks.note: a bat is a stick used in games
eaux is the French for waters, the language spoken around Quebec

explanation.surface: A cartoon Mountie's boats keep tight to the waters near Quebec.
explanation.walkthrough: Dudley Do-Right is the cartoon Canadian Mountie, so his boats are Canadian ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Bateaux are light flat-bottomed river boats used in Canada, so they suit a Canadian hero.

clue.text: Appointed to represent unfortunate lad over article

indicators.note: unfortunate suggests something gone awry, so the letters fall into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
an item is an article

explanation.surface: A hapless boy gets put in charge of some object.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad litem is legal Latin for 'for the lawsuit', describing a guardian appointed to represent someone in a case.

clue.text: Test elfin yak on base?

blocks.note: an auf is an elf's child, a changeling, so elfin offspring
to yak is to gab, chatter
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: Testing whether a dainty yak can stand on a base.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'base' is the mathematical constant, not a foundation.
explanation.definitionFit: Aufgabe is the German word for a task or exercise, used in English for a test set to students.

clue.text: Stop from holding the reins one in French compartment

blocks.note: un is French for one
a panel is a compartment or section of a surface

explanation.surface: Someone told to stop steering a French vehicle with separate compartments.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel is a pad saddle, so to unpanel is to unsaddle, ending one's riding.

clue.text: Prepared son in unusual hype about entering degree

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters take an irregular order
one thing in another sits inside it
entering means going inside, so this letter goes into the jumble

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
taken as written
c, for circa, means about
D is the abbreviation for degree

explanation.surface: A son gets ready amid strange publicity about his degree.
explanation.walkthrough: S and C both go inside a jumble of HYPE, then D follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To be psyched or psyched up is to be mentally prepared and ready for something.

clue.text: Places to stay could be fresh and exciting extensions?

blocks.note: hot means fresh and exciting, as hot news
an el is an extension or wing built at right angles to a main building

explanation.surface: Accommodation, once extended, might become new and thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'el' (from its L shape) is an American term for a building extension.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotels are establishments offering rooms for travellers to stay in.

clue.text: Crooked account concealing demand for payment

indicators.note: something concealing another hides it inside itself

blocks.note: ac is the abbreviation for account
a dun is a demand for payment of a debt

explanation.surface: A dishonest set of books hides a debt demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' suggests dishonest; here it means hooked in shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Adunc means hooked or curved inward, so bent and crooked in shape.

clue.text: In Bantu it is not about symbol next to adjective

blocks.note: a is a dictionary abbreviation for about
ikon is a variant spelling of icon, a symbol
a is the abbreviation for adjective

explanation.surface: A linguistics note: in a Bantu tongue it is not a symbol placed near an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Aikona is a South African interjection from Bantu languages meaning no, or it is not so.

clue.text: Untangling this tangle would leave Romeo glib

indicators.note: untangling sorts a knot into order, so letters are rearranged into the phrase

blocks.note: the result of the sorting, taken as written

explanation.surface: Sorting out this mess would make a lover smooth-tongued.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: the answer is the fodder, and the clue tells you its rearrangement is Romeo glib.
explanation.definitionFit: An embroglio, a variant of imbroglio, is a confused or complicated situation, a tangle.

clue.text: Death-dealing African voodoo priestess accepted for ordinary

indicators.note: one thing given for another means it replaces it

blocks.note: a mambo is a voodoo priestess
A is the abbreviation for accepted, as on a bill
O for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: A deadly African voodoo priestess is welcomed as commonplace.
explanation.walkthrough: In MAMBO, the O is swapped for A.
explanation.definitionFit: The mamba is a highly venomous African snake whose bite can kill.

clue.text: Rev supporting what implies very soft particular piece

indicators.note: in a down clue a support sits underneath, so the first-named piece is written below the second

blocks.note: BB marks a very soft pencil lead
to gun an engine is to rev it

explanation.surface: Revving an engine to back up a quiet, specific part.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supporting' puts the engine word below the pencil grade. 'Particular' plays on particles: the gun fires shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A BB gun is an air gun that fires small shot pellets, a piece (slang for a firearm) for particles.

clue.text: Macron's embarrassment extended by one who grants wishes

indicators.note: extended by means stretched to take in an extra piece

blocks.note: gêne is French for embarrassment, and Macron is the French president
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The French president's awkwardness is prolonged by a wish-granter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' does double duty: it is the numeral and also completes 'one who grants wishes'.
explanation.definitionFit: A genie in Arabian tales is a spirit that grants its master's wishes.

clue.text: Harvest turned around but for what's left in inlet

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the word is read from the back
what is at the left of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: bar means except, as does but for
the leftmost letter of inlet

explanation.surface: A crop that was turned round, apart from what remains in a creek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's left' suggests a remainder; it means the letter on the left.
explanation.definitionFit: In India and Pakistan the rabi is the spring harvest of crops sown in autumn.

clue.text: Old school inscription that's familiar to Celts

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a gam is a school of whales

explanation.surface: An ancient school carving known to the Celtic peoples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' looks like a place of learning but is a group of whales.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogam, or ogham, is an early Irish alphabet of strokes carved on standing stones.

clue.text: Shut up over well-balanced source of sugar

blocks.note: pent means shut up, confined
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
sane means sound of mind, well-balanced

explanation.surface: Be quiet about a healthy, balanced sweetener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' reads as a command to be silent; it means confined.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentosane is a polysaccharide that breaks down to yield pentose sugars.

clue.text: Papal edict sent electronically that is not bright and breezy?

blocks.note: e- as in email means sent electronically
a bull is a formal edict issued by the pope
i.e. stands for id est, that is
n't is the contracted form of not

explanation.surface: An emailed decree from the pope that is anything but cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not bright and breezy' looks negative, but 'not' is wordplay and the definition is the cheerful phrase alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebullient means overflowing with cheerful energy, lively and high-spirited.

clue.text: Miss tucking in a navy woolly

indicators.note: tucking something in puts it inside, so one piece is wrapped round the other

blocks.note: to miss a chance is to lose it
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for navy

explanation.surface: A young lady pulling on a navy-blue jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a girl and 'woolly' like a jumper (a sweater); they are a verb and an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanose is a rare word meaning woolly or covered in wool, from Latin lana.

clue.text: Postgrad able to make free ingredient for beer

indicators.note: letters set free can roam into any order

blocks.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a postgraduate degree
taken as written

explanation.surface: A graduate student able to brew beer for free.
explanation.definitionFit: Mabela is ground sorghum used in southern Africa to brew traditional beer and make porridge.
